meta_title: Zakamsk Trout Farm | Investment opportunity in western Ukraine
meta_description: An operating, spring-fed trout farm in the Carpathian foothills seeking partners to grow from 3 t to 400 t a year, in stages, from roe to market fish.
hero_title: Spring-fed Carpathian trout, from egg to table.
hero_sub: An operating family trout farm in western Ukraine, ready to grow from 3 t to 400 t a year.
hero_img_alt: The farm's two ponds and concrete dam at sunset, Carpathian foothills behind
opp_title: Ukraine imports most of its red fish.
opp1_body: About 85% of the fish eaten in Ukraine is imported. In 2025 Ukraine was one of the three largest buyers of Norwegian trout, while the country's entire aquaculture sector produced only about 16,000 t, mostly pond fish.
opp2_title: Clean water that is already here
opp2_body: The ponds are fed by underground springs next to the Limnytsia river, beside a protected landscape reserve and far from industry.
opp3_title: A short road to European buyers
opp3_body: Paved road, power and a rail line are nearby. Poland is 150 km away, with Romania, Hungary and Slovakia within 300 km.
opp_source: Sources: Norwegian Seafood Council (January 2026); Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine (February 2026); UIFSA, association of Ukrainian fish importers (January 2024).
farm_title: The farm is built and selling.
farm_lead: The ponds have been in operation since 2018 and the farm sells trout in Ukraine, about 3 t a year today. Most of the capacity is still unused. The photos below are from the site.
img_pond_alt: One of the farm ponds in summer with spring water flowing in
img_inlet_alt: Spring water pipe filling a pond over a gravel bank
img_sturgeon_alt: Handling a sturgeon beside a concrete rearing pool
img_dam_alt: Crane placing concrete slabs on the pond dam during construction
proof1: Two ponds with 1.5 to 2 m gravel beds, dam and sluices built to a regional water authority design
proof2: Registered as a trout farm in 2018, operating permit since 2019
proof3: Regular buyers in Ukraine: restaurants, resorts and households
proof4: Hydraulic works and technical documentation completed (design No. 1456-14-GR)
loop_lead: The model keeps each step on the farm, so quality is controlled from the egg to the packed fish and waste becomes an input.
loop1_body: A recirculating system (RAS) incubates eggs and raises trout and sturgeon fry.
loop2_body: Fry grow in spring-fed ponds and cages to 330 g portion trout and 1 kg fish.
loop3_body: Chilling, vacuum packing and red caviar, ready for retail and export.
loop4_body: Fry for other farms, market trout and special orders. Ukraine first, then export to Poland, Czechia, Austria and France.
loop5_body: Farm waste feeds a California red worm unit. Worm biomass supplements fish feed and the by-product is sold as organic biohumus fertiliser.
plan_lead: Investor funds are released in tranches: the hatchery is built first, then fish production grows step by step. Each stage builds on assets that already work.
img_masterplan_alt: 3D master plan of the farm with ponds, cage lines and buildings
p1_body: A recirculating system (RAS) that takes the cycle from roe to fry on the farm, so production no longer depends on bought fry.
p1_w2: Water treatment, aeration and liquid oxygen
p1_w4: First roe batches and starter feed
p1_target: Own fry for the farm and for sale
p2_body: Grow market fish in ponds and cages, add our own feed and processing, and start exporting.
p2_target: Up to 400 t of fish a year
p3_body: Guest cabins, a restaurant and sport fishing beside the ponds, with a possible second site in Poland. Income is reinvested in fish production.
p3_target: Visitor income that funds the farm
resort_title: A farm guests will travel to.
resort_lead: A traditional Carpathian restaurant, SPA and cabins beside the ponds. The cabins are not built yet, but the building materials are already on site.
img_resort_alt: Visualisation of the planned wooden restaurant, cabins and parking in winter

team_body: Founder Marian Pasternak trained on farms abroad and at a trout farm in Lviv region before choosing this site for its water. He has financed the farm himself since 2014.
press_quote: Trout is an indicator of purity. It will not live in dirty water.
risk_title: Risks, and how we manage them.
risk_lead: Serious investors ask about risk first. These are the main ones and our approach to each.
r1_a: Trout need cool water. The ponds are fed by cold underground springs, and phase 1 adds aeration and liquid oxygen for hot periods.
r2_a: Our own hatchery reduces the risk of bringing in disease with purchased fry. Water quality is monitored and veterinary control is part of the operating plan.
r3_a: The farm already sells about 3 t a year in Ukraine. Fry sales, special orders and export to four EU countries widen the customer base.
r4_a: The farm is in western Ukraine, far from the front line. Phased funding limits the capital exposed at any one time.
r5_a: Funds are released in tranches: the hatchery first, then grow-out and processing. Money for the next stage is released only when the previous one delivers.
